title: Microsoft Teams: delegators can lock calls and enable a delegate join tone
summary: The briefing's rollout details and user controls are supported by Microsoft's notice, and the administrative paths and commands are documented. The licensing statement follows the cited delegation guide, but should acknowledge that Microsoft's calling-feature comparison gives a different entitlement for basic delegate membership.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A delegator can lock an active call to prevent delegates from joining it.
claims.quote: Delegators can lock an ongoing call to prevent delegates from joining or resuming the call

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Locking prevents delegates from resuming a held call.
claims.quote:
Delegators can lock an active call to prevent delegates from:

- Resuming a call that has been placed on hold.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Delegators can optionally enable a warning tone when a delegate joins a call.
claims.quote: can optionally enable warning tones that notify participants when a delegate joins or resumes a call.

claims.claim: The enabled warning tone also sounds when a delegate resumes a held call.
claims.quote:
When enabled, all call participants will hear an audible notification when a delegate:

- Joins an active call.
- Resumes a held call.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The delegation guide says both delegator and delegate need a Teams Phone licence.
claims.quote: In the example where a manager is delegating calls to an administrative assistant, the manager and administrative assistant must each have a Teams Phone license.
claims.fix: Add after the licence paragraph: 'Microsoft's Teams Calling features comparison separately lists "Member of call group or call delegation" as available with a Microsoft Teams Enterprise licence alone, whereas the delegation guide says both parties need Teams Phone (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/here-s-what-you-get-with-phone-system#teams-calling-features).' Add that comparison URL to sources.

claims.claim: Delegation is configured at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Delegation for inbound and outbound calls.
claims.quote:
select Voice > Calling policies.
2. Choose the policy you would like to update or select Add to create a new policy.
3. Toggle Delegation for inbound and outbound calls on.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy accepts Identity and the Boolean AllowDelegation parameter to control delegation generally.
claims.quote: Enables the user to configure delegation in the Microsoft Teams client and that inbound calls to be routed to delegates; allows delegates to make outbound calls on behalf of the users for whom they have delegated permissions.

claims.claim: AllowDelegation enables delegation generally and is turned on by default.
claims.quote: You enable delegation by using the TeamsCallingPolicy AllowDelegation setting. You can use Teams admin center or Teams PowerShell. This setting is turned on by default.

claims.claim: A licensed user's call settings are reached through Teams admin center > Users > Manage users > user > Voice.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, go to Users > Manage users and select a licensed user.
6. On the user details page, go to the Voice tab.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsUserCallingDelegate accepts Identity, Delegate and the five Boolean permissions printed in the call to change an existing delegate's permissions.
claims.quote:
Set-CsUserCallingDelegate
    -Identity <String>
    -Delegate <String>
    [-MakeCalls <Boolean>]
    [-ManageSettings <Boolean>]
    [-ReceiveCalls <Boolean>]
    [-PickUpHeldCalls <Boolean>]
    [-JoinActiveCalls <Boolean>]
    [<CommonParameters>]

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: JoinActiveCalls is a per-delegate permission to join active calls, not a documented per-call lock setting.
claims.quote: Specifies whether delegate is allowed to join active calls on behalf of the specified user.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: PickUpHeldCalls is a per-delegate permission for picking up calls, not a documented warning-tone setting.
claims.quote:
### -PickUpHeldCalls

Specifies whether delegate is allowed to pick up calls on behalf of the specified user.

claims.where: controls[2]; summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI, calling policy parameter or API is documented to require the warning tone or force or disable the lock.
claims.quote: Searched: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell delegate lock call warning tone admin policy configuration default. Opened user-call-settings, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy, Set-CsUserCallingDelegate, Set-CsUserCallingSettings and Graph call delegation API overview; no such admin control.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Neither the notice nor Learn explains how the per-call lock interacts with JoinActiveCalls and PickUpHeldCalls.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Lock call" delegate; MicrosoftTeams PowerShell delegate lock call warning tone admin policy configuration default. Read MC1429012, user-call-settings and Set-CsUserCallingDelegate. None explains the interaction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning delegation off also requires cleaning up the user's delegation relationships in Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.
claims.quote: When you turn off delegation for a user, you also need to clean up delegation relationships for that user in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.

claims.claim: Learn recommends assigning delegates and delegators the same calling policy.
claims.quote: Therefore, it's recommended that delegates and delegators are assigned the same calling policy.

claims.claim: A delegate is bound to their own calling policy rather than inheriting the delegator's calling-policy permissions.
claims.quote: the delegate is bound to the settings configured in their calling policy and the permissions of the delegator's calling policy are not transferred to the delegate.

claims.claim: The notice recommends evaluating whether to recommend the tone for users handling confidential or sensitive conversations.
